blogs.title: Reviving LSTMs with Exponential Gating: How a Simple Change Fixes Forgetting
blogs.description: An easy‑to‑follow explanation of exponential gating, why classic LSTMs struggle to revise stored information, and how turning sigmoid gates into exponential ones lets the network ‘rewrite’ its memory on the fly. The post uses everyday analogies (like updating a sticky note) and walks through the stabilisation tricks that keep the math from blowing up.

blogs.title: sLSTM Explained: Scalar Memory Meets Smart Mixing for Better State Tracking
blogs.description: A layperson’s guide to the new sLSTM variant. It covers the concept of a single‑value cell state, introduces the normalizer that keeps track of gate strength, and shows how “memory mixing” across multiple heads lets the model remember complex patterns such as parity checks—something vanilla Transformers can’t do.

blogs.title: mLSTM Unlocked: From Tiny Scalars to Full‑Size Matrix Memories
blogs.description: Describes how expanding the cell from a single number to a matrix gives the network a built‑in ‘key‑value store’. The post explains the covariance update rule (think of adding flashcards to a notebook), why this yields massive storage capacity, and how exponential gates become learning rates for these updates.

blogs.title: Building xLSTM Blocks: Marrying Classic RNNs with Modern Residual Architectures
blogs.description: Shows how the authors embed sLSTM or mLSTM cells inside residual blocks with up‑projection layers—mirroring what Transformers do but keeping computation linear in sequence length. The article walks through post‑up‑projection vs. pre‑up‑projection designs and why they matter for speed and accuracy.

blogs.title: Scaling Recurrent Networks to Billions of Parameters: What xLSTM Achieves on Language Modeling Benchmarks
blogs.description: Presents the experimental side of the paper in an accessible story format. It compares validation perplexities of xLSTM against GPT‑3‑style Transformers, State‑Space Models, and RWKV/RNN variants on 15B – 300B token training runs, highlighting how xLSTM consistently outperforms them and follows favorable scaling laws.

blogs.title: Why xLSTM Could Be Your Next Choice for Fast, Low‑Memory Text Generation
blogs.description: "Beyond accuracy" – this post dives into practical benefits such as constant‑memory inference, linear generation time versus quadratic Transformer slowdown, higher throughput at large batch sizes, and current limitations like non‑parallelizable sLSTM steps or heavy CUDA kernels. It also outlines future engineering work needed to make xLSTM production‑ready.
